label: Position and Movement
text: Chapter 9: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement
text: Scalars and vectors, motion graphs, equations of motion and free fall. Key points are summarised below, followed by worked examples with full solutions and the original scanned notes.

label: Position and Movement
text: Revision Notes

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.1 Scalar and vector

label: Position and Movement
text: A scalar has magnitude only (distance, speed, mass, density). A vector has magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, acceleration, force).

label: Position and Movement
text: Adding vectors gives a resultant. Parallel vectors in the same direction add; in opposite directions they subtract. Non-parallel vectors use the tip-to-tail method.

label: Position and Movement
text: View notes p.1

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.2 Distance and displacement

label: Position and Movement
text: Distance is the length of the path taken (scalar). Displacement is the shortest distance from the start to the final position (vector) and does not depend on the path.

label: Position and Movement
text: Both have the SI unit metre (m).

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.3 Speed and velocity

label: Position and Movement
text: Speed = distance travelled per unit time. Velocity = displacement per unit time. Unit: m s⁻¹.

label: Position and Movement
text: Average speed = total distance ÷ time taken. Average velocity = total displacement ÷ time taken.

label: Position and Movement
text: Change in velocity Δv = v − u, found by vector subtraction.

label: Position and Movement
text: View notes p.2

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.4 Uniform motion

label: Position and Movement
text: An object is in uniform motion when it travels with constant velocity: both its speed and its direction stay unchanged.

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.5 Acceleration

label: Position and Movement
text: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v − u) ÷ t. It is a vector with unit m s⁻², and its direction is shown by the sign + or −.

label: Position and Movement
text: An object accelerates when its speed and/or its direction changes.

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.6 Motion graphs

label: Position and Movement
text: Slope of an s-t graph = velocity. Slope of a v-t graph = acceleration. Area under a v-t graph = displacement. Area under an a-t graph = change in velocity.

label: Position and Movement
text: Uniform motion: s-t is a straight line and v-t is horizontal. Uniform acceleration: s-t is a curve, v-t is a sloping straight line and a-t is horizontal.

label: Position and Movement
text: View notes p.3 View notes p.4

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.7 Equations of uniformly accelerated motion

label: Position and Movement
text: v = u + at s = ½(u + v)t s = ut + ½at² v² = u² + 2as

label: Position and Movement
text: These apply only to straight-line motion with constant acceleration.

label: Position and Movement
text: Over a time interval, average velocity equals the instantaneous velocity at the middle of the interval.

label: Position and Movement
text: View notes p.5

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.8 Vertical motion in air

label: Position and Movement
text: Under gravity only, an object accelerates towards the Earth at g ≈ 9.81 m s⁻². Motion going up and coming down is symmetric: equal times between two heights and equal speed at the same height.

label: Position and Movement
text: Air resistance opposes motion and grows with speed, so acceleration decreases. When weight equals air resistance, acceleration is zero and the object falls at its terminal velocity.

label: Position and Movement
text: View notes p.5 View notes p.6 View notes p.7

label: Position and Movement
text: 9.9 Devices used for recording motion

label: Position and Movement
text: A data-logging system has an interface, computer software and sensors (e.g. a motion sensor). It measures very short time changes accurately and plots s-t, v-t and a-t graphs.

label: Position and Movement
text: Stroboscopy uses flashes of adjustable frequency f to record images on one photo. The time between images is 1/f, and each image's distance from the first is the displacement.

label: Position and Movement
text: View notes p.7 View notes p.8

label: Force and Motion
text: Chapter 10: Force and Motion

label: Force and Motion
text: Newton's three laws, forces, free-body diagrams, moments and centre of gravity. Key points are summarised below, followed by worked examples with full solutions and the original scanned notes.

label: Force and Motion
text: Revision Notes

label: Force and Motion
text: 10.1 Newton's First Law of motion

label: Force and Motion
text: An object stays at rest or moves in a straight line at uniform speed if there is no net (unbalanced) force on it. Force is the cause of changes in motion.

label: Force and Motion
text: Inertia is the tendency to resist changes in motion and is measured by mass.

label: Force and Motion
text: View notes p.14

label: Force and Motion
text: 10.2 Forces

label: Force and Motion
text: Force is a vector measured in newtons (N). Forces add by the tip-to-tail or parallelogram method, or algebraically.

label: Force and Motion
text: Two perpendicular forces: F = √(F₁² + F₂²), with tan θ = F₂ ÷ F₁. Resolving a force: Fₓ = F cos θ and Fᵧ = F sin θ.

label: Force and Motion
text: Friction opposes velocity and is independent of speed and contact area. Fluid resistance opposes velocity, grows with speed and is smaller for streamlined shapes. Weight is the Earth's pull, always vertically downward. Normal reaction acts perpendicular to the contact surface.

label: Force and Motion
text: A free-body diagram shows every force on an object, with arrow direction and length showing direction and magnitude.

label: Force and Motion
text: View notes p.14 View notes p.15 View notes p.16 View notes p.17

label: Force and Motion
text: 10.3 Newton's Second Law of motion

label: Force and Motion
text: A net force makes an object accelerate in the direction of that force. The acceleration is proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to mass: F = ma.

label: Force and Motion
text: On a horizontal surface, normal reaction cancels weight (R = mg). On an incline, resolve weight into mg sin θ along the plane and mg cos θ perpendicular to it (R = mg cos θ).

label: Force and Motion
text: View notes p.17 View notes p.18

label: Force and Motion
text: 10.4 Newton's Third Law of motion

label: Force and Motion
text: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. If A exerts a force on B, B exerts a force of equal magnitude and opposite direction on A.

label: Force and Motion
text: Action and reaction act on different objects, e.g. Earth and object, ground and object, tension between blocks, rocket and exhaust gas.

label: Force and Motion
text: View notes p.19

label: Force and Motion
text: 10.5 Moment of a force

label: Force and Motion
text: Moment of a force about a point = perpendicular component of force × distance = F sin θ × r (unit: N m). It measures the turning effect.

label: Force and Motion
text: A couple is two equal and opposite forces: zero resultant force but a turning effect Fd. Torque is the net moment of a couple.

label: Force and Motion
text: An object is in equilibrium when the net force is zero and total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment.

label: Force and Motion
text: View notes p.20

label: Force and Motion
text: 10.6 Centre of gravity

label: Force and Motion
text: The centre of gravity is the point where all the weight can be considered to act. For point masses: x_cg = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂ + …) ÷ (m₁ + m₂ + …).

label: Force and Motion
text: A uniform rod has its centre of gravity at its mid-point. An object made of two uniform parts can be treated as two point masses.

label: Force and Motion
text: View notes p.21

label: Glossary
text: Glossary

label: Glossary
text: Key definitions from the notes in one place.

label: Glossary
text: Scalar

label: Glossary
text: A quantity with magnitude only, e.g. distance, speed, mass, density.

label: Glossary
text: Vector

label: Glossary
text: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, e.g. displacement, velocity, acceleration, force.

label: Glossary
text: Resultant

label: Glossary
text: The single vector produced when two or more vectors are added.

label: Glossary
text: Distance

label: Glossary
text: The length of the path taken by an object. It is a scalar.

label: Glossary
text: Displacement

label: Glossary
text: The shortest distance from the starting position to the final position. It is a vector and is independent of the path.

label: Glossary
text: Speed

label: Glossary
text: Distance travelled per unit time.

label: Glossary
text: Velocity

label: Glossary
text: Displacement per unit time; it tells how fast and in which direction an object moves.

label: Glossary
text: Uniform motion

label: Glossary
text: Motion with constant velocity: speed and direction both stay unchanged.

label: Glossary
text: Acceleration

label: Glossary
text: The rate of change of velocity, a = (v − u) ÷ t. Unit: m s⁻².

label: Glossary
text: Acceleration due to gravity (g)

label: Glossary
text: The constant acceleration of an object under gravity only, about 9.81 m s⁻² towards the Earth.

label: Glossary
text: Air resistance

label: Glossary
text: The force exerted by the air that opposes the motion of a moving object. It increases with speed.

label: Glossary
text: Terminal velocity

label: Glossary
text: The constant velocity reached when the weight of a falling object is balanced by air resistance.

label: Glossary
text: Data-logging system

label: Glossary
text: A system of sensors, an interface and computer software that records time-varying data and shows it as graphs and tables.

label: Glossary
text: Stroboscopy

label: Glossary
text: A method of capturing images of fast-moving objects using intense flashes at an adjustable frequency.

label: Glossary
text: Force

label: Glossary
text: A vector measured in newtons (N). An unbalanced force changes an object's speed and/or direction.

label: Glossary
text: Net force

label: Glossary
text: The resultant of all forces acting on an object; also called the unbalanced force.

label: Glossary
text: Inertia

label: Glossary
text: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. It is measured by mass.

label: Glossary
text: Friction

label: Glossary
text: A force opposite to the direction of motion, independent of speed and of the area in contact.

label: Glossary
text: Weight

label: Glossary
text: The force exerted on an object by the Earth, always directed vertically downward.

label: Glossary
text: Normal reaction

label: Glossary
text: The force perpendicular to the contact surface when two objects press against each other.

label: Glossary
text: Free-body diagram

label: Glossary
text: A diagram showing all the forces acting on one object, drawn as arrows.

label: Glossary
text: Moment of a force

label: Glossary
text: The turning effect of a force about a point: perpendicular component of the force × distance from the point (N m).

label: Glossary
text: Couple

label: Glossary
text: Two equal forces acting in opposite directions. The resultant force is zero but there is a turning effect.

label: Glossary
text: Torque

label: Glossary
text: The net moment of force produced by a couple.

label: Glossary
text: Equilibrium

label: Glossary
text: A state with no translational or rotational acceleration: zero net force and balanced clockwise and anticlockwise moments.

label: Glossary
text: Centre of gravity

label: Glossary
text: The point where all the weight of an object can be considered to be concentrated.
